text:
The neighbor would most likely recover for negligence: gasoline and oil residue left on the shop floor where a repair spark could ignite it was a failure of reasonable care, and the smoke damage to the house was a foreseeable result. Trespass does not lie, because the mechanic did not intend the smoke to enter the neighbor’s land. A routine auto-repair fire is not an abnormally dangerous activity, so strict liability does not apply.

CONFIDENCE: 74
